newsitem.title: UK: Thistle Hotels sets slim premium on debut.
newsitem.headline: Thistle Hotels sets slim premium on debut.

text.p: Shares in Thistle Hotels Plc set a slim premium on their issue price in active trading on Wednesday as the stock made its debut on the London exchange.

By 0805 GMT Thistle -- the second largest UK hotels group -- was quoted at 172-1/2p, compared with the offer price of 170p, confirmed earlier in a statement from the company's 46.0 percent shareholder Brierley Investments of New Zealand.

Volume in Thistle reached 5.8 million shares, making it the most actively traded UK stock. The company raised some 237.6 million stg through the offering, which gave it a market value of some 1.05 million stg.

A spokesman for the company said it was "gratified" to be trading at a premium to the issue price but that the company's true value was expected to emerge over coming weeks and months rather than in the first few hours of dealing.
"What we wanted to do in the offering was ensure we got the right shareholder base and that we have succeeded in doing," the spokesman said.
He said some two-thirds of the stock on offer had been bought by UK investors and a third was sold to international investors.

Thistle's 170p issue price was at the low end of the price range between 170p and 210p initially set by Brierley, but comes after a spate of initial public offerings by UK hotel companies that some analysts feared would create a glut in the market.

Hotel operators have benefitted from the recent recovery in UK business and consumer activity after a lengthy downturn, and interest in the sector was given a further boost by Granada Group's bid for Forte -- the UK's biggest hotel group.
Yet analysts said Thistle had looked expensive at the upper end of the suggested price range.

"The general perception was that it was quite an expensive offering on measures such as cash flow, historic return on capital and normalised earnings before depreciation and tax," said Fraser Ramzan, analyst at Lehman Brothers.
Thistle said it would have paid a dividend of 3.7p in the past year if its shares had been listed.

That would give a yield of 2.4 percent at today's issue price -- below the average 3.75 percent for the UK stock market as a whole, but in line with the hotel and leisure sector at 2.76 percent and rival Stakis at 2.5 percent.
Thistle chief executive Robert Peel said the company was delighted at making its return to the London market and that the capital raised would provide an excellent platform for growth.
"The group's strengthened financial position will support the ongoing refurbishment and upgrading of the group's portfolio and the expansion of room capacity," Peel said.
Thistle has 100 hotels with over 13,500 rooms, including 24 hotels in London and 25 in Scotland.
The company said retail investors would have the first 1,000 stg of the applications met in full and would be allocated 75 percent of the balance.
Unconditional dealings in the stock start on October 9.
